synthesis.intent_alignment: The primary intent mix (commercial 0.408 / navigational 0.325 / informational 0.235) shows searchers are comparing local house-cleaning providers to shortlist and contact one directly, so the page needs to read as a decision aid (pricing, trust signals, service area, direct booking) rather than generic informational content about cleaning.
competitor_takeaways: Jim's Cleaning dominates trust signalling with 3,096 reviews at 4.8 — volume of reviews is the single biggest credibility gap the client must close with narrative trust signals (dedicated team, guarantees, 24/7 Clean membership) since it cannot compete on review count yet
Several competitors price-anchor directly on the page (Mum and Me 'From $132', Inner City Maids 'with prices') — omitting a price signal risks looking evasive next to these listings

Personal, named-operator framing (Frank at Greenlight, Chad at United Home Services) reads as more locally credible than faceless brand copy — worth mirroring with Zoe Brauer as founder/face of the Bentleigh service
Multiple competitors treat Bentleigh and Bentleigh East as one combined service area rather than siloing them, which matches actual local search behaviour (see related searches)

PAA results skew toward generic/international cleaning-cost content (UK, US) rather than Bentleigh-specific answers — a well-targeted local FAQ answering 'how much do house cleaners charge per hour in Australia' with Melbourne-specific figures is a content gap the client can win outright
